result.title: What Happens Inside the World's Most Advanced Factories?
result.description:
What does the factory of the future actually look like?

In this documentary, we travel to Viet Nam, Türkiye and the United States to step inside three leading manufacturing facilities recognized by the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse Network.

From AI-assisted production and workforce training to renewable energy and resource efficiency, we explore how companies including Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII), @beko and @ericsson are rethinking the way factories operate.

What we found wasn't just new technology – it was people learning, adapting and helping shape the future of manufacturing.

To find out how over two hundred Global Lighthouses are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and forging a path forward for industries, follow this link: https://initiatives.weforum.org/global-lighthouse-network/home

result.title: These countries are leading the energy transition in 2026
result.description:
The energy transition is underway. But progress around the world is uneven. Which countries are furthest ahead? And which are catching up the fastest?

The Energy Transition Index benchmarks the progress of 120 countries towards a more secure, equitable and sustainable energy future. Familiar names are at the top this year, but there is notable progress elsewhere, as Roberto Bocca, Head of the Forum’s Centre for Energy and Materials, explains.

result.title: A “fundamental shift” in energy thinking: the Energy Transition Index 2026
result.description:
The World Economic Forum's Energy Transition Index has been charting the progress of global energy systems for the last 16 years.
The latest edition is published as the world is experiencing a huge energy shock due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. We discuss what is helping and what is impeding the global transition to cleaner, more secure, more equitable energy.
Guests:
Lucy Craig, Director of Growth, Innovation, and Digitalization, DNV
Boqiang Lin, Chair Professor, School of Management, Xiamen University

Robin Pomeroy, host Radio Davos; Nicholas Wagner, Manager, Energy Initiatives, World Economic Forum

result.description:

result.title: Ghana's First Marine Sanctuary & Indigenous Forest Protection | WEF | Top Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:16 - Ghana's first marine sanctuary: Almost 200 countries across the world have pledged to protect 30% of their ocean by 2030. But right now, there’s a lot of work to do, with just 10% of the global ocean protected. #Ghana just took a big step forward with the establishment of the Greater Cape Three Points marine protected area.

01.56 - AI satellites re-shaping Earth observation: Orbitworks plans to launch a 10-satellite constellation later this year. Rather than capturing images in orbit and transmitting them back to Earth for analysis, which creates a time lag, the satellites will use #AI to process data directly in space. CEO Hamdullah Mohib is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader. Here, he explains how the technology works.

04.24 - Japan's new word for extreme heat: In 2007, Japanese weather forecasters began to use a new word - ‘moshobi’, meaning extremely hot day - to describe when the mercury climbed past 35˚C. 

05.53 - Empowering indigenous forest protection: Indigenous cultures have a lot to teach the world, says Indonesian rainforest activist Bustar Maitar. And the first thing is to respect nature by taking from it only what you need. Maitar enjoyed a successful career with Greenpeace, winning ‘zero deforestation’ pledges from major multinationals. But he was drawn back to Papua to fight for forests there - and also, through his EcoNusa Foundation, to defend the rights, culture and livelihoods of #Indigenous communities, from which will emerge the next generation of #forest stewards.
